speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the written Question No 24 by Dr Tan Wu Meng in today's Order Paper.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The proportion with active symptoms was lower, at 2.1%.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Members raised concerns about individuals being denied health insurance coverage due to their mental health conditions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is a valid concern and should be considered within the larger context of our S+3M healthcare safety net system.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: All Singaporeans are eligible for healthcare subsidies of up to 80% in public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MSHL is sized to cover nine in 10 bills in the subsidised wards of public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Beyond subsidies and MSHL, individuals can also buy private Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and other insurance plans.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Insurers should carry out an objective assessment of every application, based on reliable information or data relevant to the risks being insured.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Where an application is rejected or approved with higher premiums or additional conditions, insurers should properly explain to the customer the basis for the underwriting decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We want to allow Ms He to also ask her supplementary question.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister if he would consider one suggestion?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would MOH look into setting up a website portal so that members of the public can provide authenticated experiences of their dealings with insurance companies, including when the company is unreasonable in refusing to provide insurance coverage, such as in the case of the person, a member of the public, Tan Hui In, who, in The Straits Times Forum in July, mentioned how their daughter had bipolar disorder but got turned away by two large insurance companies?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These are experiences that the public can, indeed, share.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I think the larger point is, perhaps, should we take into account complaints or concerns expressed by members of the public and how they have been dealt with by their insurance companies and use that in some way to inform the public.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I will take it back to my colleagues in MOH and we will study to see how this can be used to improve conditions for all the insured.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First, I noticed that the Senior Minister of State quoted data from the 2016 Mental Health Survey that was conducted.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering whether a more up-to-date survey is in the works, given that with increased awareness and after COVID-19, we could actually see a difference in the number of individuals who are diagnosed with mental health conditions and illnesses.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Second, does the Ministry consider these issues about ostensible denial of insurance coverage?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Does the Minister consider this to be a problem or is the Ministry working with MAS at the moment to study whether this is an issue and how many individuals this might actually be affecting and whether or not further remedial action needs to be taken to make sure that insurers are not discriminating against these individuals?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
